entry.author: Sport New Zealand Ihi Aotearoa
entry.summary:
This session brings practical examples of collaboration and innovation already underway across the sector.  It shows how organisations are responding to growing pressure by partnering differently, building shared capability, and finding smarter ways to work across regional and national layers.  Facilitated by Jim Ellis, Sport NZ

Athletics NZ – Cam Mitchell, CEOAthletics NZ offers an example of a national body rebuilding regional capability by working more closely with Regional Sports Trusts. The session will explore how clearer roles, stronger regional connections and practical partnership can help extend reach and better support clubs, coaches and communities.

Northland Sports Coalition – Janine Moy (Systems lead, Sport Northland), Dave Mullan (Club Development Officer, North Golf Association)This coalition shows what can happen when regional organisations choose to align effort, reduce duplication and tackle common challenges together. It offers a practical example of a coalition model designed to strengthen coordination, collective voice and regional impact.

Regional Sports Trust (RST) Network Project – Vanessa Hughey-Pol (CEO Active Southland), Heidi Lichtwark (CEO Sport Bay of Plenty), Brent Eastwood (RST Network Director)The RST Network Project highlights the value of Regional Sports Trusts working more intentionally as a network rather than as separate regions solving the same problems alone. It demonstrates how shared tools, learning and coordinated approaches can build capability, reduce rework and lift consistency across the system.
